title: Identification through continuous health and location monitoring
description: Continuous collection of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps can be used to identify the user's identity, daily routines, home/work locations, and health status, potentially revealing sensitive personal information beyond the intended purpose.

title: Disclosure of sensitive health and location data
description: Sensor telemetry data including heart rate, GPS position, and health metrics could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through data breaches, insecure transmission, or improper access controls, violating user privacy expectations.

title: Linkability of data across time and contexts
description: Continuous sensor data can be linked across different time periods and contexts to create comprehensive user profiles, potentially correlating health patterns with location data to infer sensitive activities or conditions.

title: Data manipulation of sensor telemetry
description: Sensor data could be altered, tampered with, or falsified during collection or transmission, compromising data integrity and potentially leading to incorrect health assessments or misleading location tracking.

title: Individual identification from GPS traces and device ID
description: GPS traces and device identifiers transmitted from the wearable device can be used to identify specific individuals and track their movements, potentially revealing sensitive location patterns and personal habits.

title: Linkability of wearable data with other data sources
description: Exercise session data, GPS traces, and timestamps could be linked with other personal data sources (e.g., health records, social media, other apps) to create comprehensive user profiles that reveal more than intended.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health and location data
description: The companion mobile app may store sensitive health data, GPS traces, and device identifiers that could be accessed by unauthorized parties through app vulnerabilities, data breaches, or improper access controls.

title: Data manipulation during transmission
description: Sensor data, GPS traces, and timestamps could be altered during transmission from the wearable device to the companion app, potentially leading to inaccurate health records or misleading location information.

title: Device identity usurpation
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the wearable device or user identity to gain unauthorized access to the companion app, potentially accessing or manipulating user data.

title: Linkability of health data across contexts
description: Calorie, meal, and weight data logged by the user could be linked to their identity across different systems or time periods, potentially revealing patterns about their lifestyle, health status, or daily routines.
assumptions: Data is stored in a centralized system accessible by multiple parties

title: Identification of user from health data
description: Unique combinations of weight entries, meal patterns, and calorie intake could potentially be used to identify the specific user, especially if combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Data is stored in a way that allows cross-referencing with other datasets

title: Unauthorized disclosure of personal health data
description: The companion mobile app could disclose the user's calorie, meal, and weight data to unauthorized third parties through data breaches, improper sharing, or inadequate access controls.
assumptions: The app has network connectivity and data sharing capabilities

title: Usurpation of user identity for data logging
description: An unauthorized person could gain access to the user's companion app and log calorie, meal, and weight data on behalf of the user, potentially leading to inaccurate health records and privacy violations.
assumptions: The app has authentication mechanisms that could be bypassed or compromised

title: Health Log Identifiability
description: Health logs containing calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions can directly identify the user through unique patterns and personal health data.
assumptions: Health data is personally identifiable and can be correlated with user identity

title: Health Log Linkability
description: Health log data can be linked to other data sources (e.g., social media, fitness trackers) to create comprehensive user profiles.
assumptions: Cross-platform data sharing and integration is possible

title: Unauthorized Health Log Disclosure
description: Health logs stored in DS1 could be accessed by unauthorized parties through security vulnerabilities, insider threats, or inadequate access controls.
assumptions: Data store may have insufficient security measures

title: Health Log Data Integrity Compromise
description: Health logs could be tampered with, modified, or deleted by unauthorized actors, leading to inaccurate health records.
assumptions: Data store may lack proper integrity controls

title: Health Log Usurpation
description: Unauthorized users could impersonate legitimate users to access or modify their health logs through weak authentication mechanisms.
assumptions: Authentication may be insufficient to prevent impersonation

title: Location Linkability
description: GPS location traces with timestamps can be used to link different activities, locations, and time periods together, potentially revealing patterns about the user's daily routine, social interactions, and movements.

title: Sensitive Information Inference
description: Location history data can be analyzed to infer sensitive personal information such as home address, workplace, religious practices, medical visits, political affiliations, or other private activities based on location patterns.

title: Unauthorized Location Data Disclosure
description: Location history data stored in DS2 could be accessed by unauthorized parties through security breaches, improper access controls, or insider threats, leading to privacy violations.

title: Location Data Integrity Compromise
description: Location traces stored in DS2 could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted by malicious actors, leading to inaccurate location records or false location data.

title: Privacy Control Usability
description: Users may find it difficult to manage, review, or delete their location history data, leading to unintended privacy exposure or lack of control over personal location information.

title: Health Log Identifiability Risk
description: The Health Analytics Service processes calorie, weight, and exercise logs that contain personally identifiable health information. Even with anonymization attempts, the combination of health metrics across multiple sessions could enable re-identification of individuals through pattern matching or cross-referencing with other data sources.
assumptions: The analytics service has access to complete historical health data across sessions, and there may be insufficient de-identification measures in place.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a reasonable fit for identifiability threats in health data processing contexts.

title: Unauthorized Health Data Disclosure
description: The Health Analytics Service may inadvertently or maliciously disclose sensitive health information to unauthorized parties. This could occur through improper access controls, data leakage during processing, or insufficient encryption of data in transit or at rest.
assumptions: The analytics service may not have adequate access controls or encryption mechanisms protecting health data during processing and storage.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 represents disclosure risks in data processing contexts.

title: Health Data Linkability Across Sessions
description: Multiple sessions of health logs (calorie, weight, exercise) can be linked together to create a comprehensive health profile of an individual. This linkability enables tracking of health trends and behaviors over time, potentially revealing sensitive health conditions or lifestyle patterns.
assumptions: The analytics service processes health data across multiple sessions without sufficient session isolation or pseudonymization.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 addresses linkability concerns in longitudinal health data processing.

title: Health Log Data Manipulation
description: The Health Analytics Service could be vulnerable to data manipulation attacks where calorie, weight, or exercise log data is altered, deleted, or falsified. This could lead to incorrect health-condition analysis and potentially harmful medical recommendations.
assumptions: The analytics service may lack adequate data integrity controls, audit trails, or tamper-detection mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 covers data manipulation risks in processing contexts.

title: Health Data Processing Non-Compliance
description: The Health Analytics Service may fail to comply with health data protection regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) when processing sensitive health information. This could result in legal penalties, loss of trust, and regulatory sanctions.
assumptions: The analytics service may not have proper compliance frameworks, consent mechanisms, or data governance policies in place.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Nc.1.1 addresses non-compliance risks in health data processing contexts.

title: Location History Linkability
description: Location history data from DS2 can be linked to specific individuals across multiple sessions, enabling tracking of individual movements and associations with other data sources.
assumptions: Data is not properly anonymized or pseudonymized before storage or transmission.

title: Movement Pattern Identification
description: Derived daily routine and movement patterns from location history can be used to identify individuals even without explicit identifiers, as unique behavioral signatures emerge.
assumptions: Analytics service has access to sufficient historical data to establish identifiable patterns.

title: Unauthorized Location Data Disclosure
description: Location history and derived movement patterns may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through security vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches in the analytics service.
assumptions: Analytics service lacks adequate access controls or encryption for sensitive location data.

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: Collecting location history across all sessions may exceed what is necessary for deriving daily routine patterns, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Analytics service collects more granular location data than required for the stated purpose.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance Risk
description: Processing of location history data may violate privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) due to sensitive nature of location data and lack of proper consent mechanisms.
assumptions: Data processing does not have adequate legal basis or user consent for location tracking.

title: Linkability of Health Insights to Other Data Sources
description: Inferred health insights (risk indicators, routine summaries, trend flags) transmitted from the Health Analytics Service could be linked with other data sources (e.g., insurance records, medical history, device usage patterns) to create a comprehensive user profile, potentially revealing sensitive health information beyond the intended scope.

title: Identifiability of Users Through Health Condition Indicators
description: Health-condition risk indicators and trend flags may contain quasi-identifying information that, when combined with other available data, could be used to identify specific individuals, violating user anonymity expectations.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Health Analytics Data
description: Inferred health insights transmitted to the Companion Mobile App could be exposed to unauthorized parties through security vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or interception during transmission, leading to privacy breaches of sensitive health information.

title: Excessive Inference of Health Information Beyond Stated Purpose
description: The Health Analytics Service may infer and transmit health-related insights (risk indicators, trend flags) that exceed the minimum necessary data required for the stated purpose of providing routine summaries, violating data minimization principles.

title: Potential Non-Compliance with Health Data Regulations
description: Transmission of inferred health insights may violate regulatory requirements such as HIPAA or GDPR if proper consent mechanisms, data protection measures, and user rights (e.g., right to access, rectification) are not adequately implemented.

title: Unauthorized Data Access by Cloud Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider (EE2) may have unauthorized access to the full health and location dataset, analytics data, and models. As a third-party external entity, there is a risk that the provider's internal security controls may be insufficient to prevent unauthorized personnel from accessing sensitive health data.

title: Data Tampering by Cloud Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider (EE2) could potentially modify, alter, or corrupt the health data, location data, analytics data, and models during storage or replication. As an external entity, there is a risk of intentional or accidental data modification without proper audit controls.

title: Unintended Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: The cloud hosting provider (EE2) may inadvertently or intentionally disclose health and location data to unauthorized third parties, including other cloud service providers, government agencies, or malicious actors. This could occur through data breaches, improper access controls, or data sharing agreements.

title: Individual Identification from Health Data
description: The full health and location dataset hosted at the cloud provider (EE2) may contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify specific individuals. Even with anonymization attempts, the combination of health records and location data could enable re-identification of individuals.

title: Linkability of Health and Location Data
description: The health and location data hosted at the cloud provider (EE2) could be linked across different datasets or time periods, potentially revealing patterns about individuals' health behaviors, movements, and medical history that were not intended to be correlated.
